sections.title: Sound and timing
sections.text: The synth has no envelope of its own: its level is the level of your exhale, so it swells, holds and stops exactly as you breathe. How long you breathe sets the echo and reverb tails, from short after a quick puff to about five times longer after a breath of four seconds or more. Short wobbles inside one exhale do not end it. If your input only shows a jump when a breath starts and another when it stops, the first jump switches a steady amplifier on and the opposite jump switches it off. Everything is in E minor: grains come from a chord bed plus the captured breath, while a second voice plays random notes of E natural minor in the instrument's own waveform; both then pass through drive, filter, chorus, echo and reverb. Motion, pump and arpeggios follow each instrument's own tempo (66–160 BPM), not the outside session; a new breath after silence restarts them on the downbeat. HYPER clips by design. Silence stays silent. The microphone is read raw, without noise suppression or echo cancellation, so keep the speaker away from it or use headphones; hold K4 if the sound starts feeding back.

sections.title: Recording
sections.text: The microphone keeps sound only while you hold. A take lands where the playhead was, is levelled to the loop's loudness and loops in time; a new take replaces it, and holds under 0.15 s are ignored. On release the Mac renders a new loop from what you hear, the loop and take at the BLEND mix, and every later loop does the same; E3 Variation sets how far it strays. Echo cancellation is off unless set in Device > Audio, so a take also hears the speaker. The waveform shows the loop in orange and the take in teal, live while recording; STATUS shows the mic level.

sections.text: Draft saved means your current workspace will reopen here. Save Visual adds a reusable version to My Visuals; Update Visual replaces that saved version. If a save is not confirmed, keep the App open and use Check Save.

sections.title: Sources and tracking
sections.text: Includes all 63 visuals with hand, face and body tracking. Choose local camera/audio inputs or image/audio WebSocket channels below the preview. The tracking kind is shown beside the image input it uses. Local inputs run on the device; maker Preview uses silent audio and isolated channels. AI creation and applying to a Viewer are not included.

sections.title: Leave and return
sections.text: Open the My Apps menu to Exit. Launch this App again to restore the last confirmed workspace. K1 remains reserved for the system menu.

sections.title: Silencing it
sections.text: Three gates in order: repeat a hidden three-key order shown for three seconds, turn E1 to the answer of a two-step sum, then hold K2 and K4 together for six seconds while keeping E2 inside a narrow window. Every mistake adds an eight-second lockout and makes the ring louder and faster. There is no snooze.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: Tasks are regenerated after every mistake, so a task cannot be memorised. If you do not touch anything for twenty seconds the ring escalates on its own. The App only counts down while it is open in the foreground, and the shell Menu can still exit it.

sections.title: Saved settings

sections.title: Sound
sections.text: Six sine operators per voice routed by one of 32 algorithms, each with ratio, detune, output level and a four-rate, four-level envelope; one operator feeds back on itself. Sixteen voices; the bass is a separate voice an octave below the chord.

sections.title: Pitch and intervals
sections.text: Twelve semitones make an octave; 100 cents make a semitone. +7 is a perfect fifth up, −5 a perfect fourth down, and ±12 an octave. E3 fine-tunes against another instrument. A middle mix combines dry and shifted audio; 0% passes only the dry input.

sections.title: Key detection
sections.text: The display shows the detected major/minor key and confidence. Twelve bars show pitch-class energy, with the root highlighted. Stable detection avoids rapid switching between related keys. Single notes, drums or noise may show Key unclear. The shifted output key is shown when applicable.

sections.title: Audio and latency
sections.text: Pitch analysis adds latency, roughly 25 ms in this design; actual device I/O adds its own delay. Headphones help prevent feedback. Mixing in dry audio can add body. Large shifts may soften low frequencies.

sections.title: Saved settings
sections.text: Pitch, fine tuning, mix, volume and bypass save automatically. Exiting releases audio input and output.

guide.description: A vocal channel with preamp gain, denoising, pitch correction, distortion and OTT compression.

Input gain: 0–60 dB, in 3 dB steps.
Pitch-correction amount: 0–100%; higher values pull harder toward the target.
Tuning speed: 0–100%; lower values sound more gradual.
Output volume: 0–120%.

Noise-learning threshold: −80 to −20 dB. Audio below it during pauses is treated as noise.

sections.title: Tuning and key
sections.text: The top display shows detected pitch and its correction target. A check mark means it is on target. Correction works on monophonic vocals; chords, drums and noise can confuse detection. Toggle Tune off on Main when needed.

sections.title: Audio and latency
sections.text: The pitch-analysis window is 10.7 ms and DSP processing is about 11 ms; total latency depends on device I/O. Spectral denoising learns the background during pauses, while the gate reduces residual noise. Set the threshold near the noise floor, then speak and pause. High preamp gain also amplifies noise. Use headphones to avoid feedback.

sections.title: Saved settings
sections.text: Parameters, current page, tuning key and module switches save automatically. Exiting releases audio input and output.

sections.title: Audio and limits
sections.text: Notes are scheduled on the audio thread at sample boundaries. Six tracks share 64 voices; the oldest voice is stolen when needed. The SF2 samples, layers, loops and envelopes are used, but SF2 filters and LFO modulation are not implemented. GM drum keys include 36 kick, 38 snare and 42 closed hat.

sections.title: Sound
sections.text: Auto-play moves through dawn, bloom, canopy, glitch and petal fall over progressions with 7ths and 9ths in any of 12 major or minor keys; in minor, every progression is re-voiced in the parallel minor. It plays a felt-piano or glass melody, glass arpeggios, vocal chops and choir, organic percussion and quantized glitches, with sidechain pump and shimmer. The holographic flower, crystals, butterflies and water ripples follow every note, glitch, freeze and section.

sections.title: Saved settings
sections.text: Specimen, page, key and all parameters save automatically; changing specimen keeps your key. Choosing a specimen loads its sound, tempo and chords. Auto-play resumes after a reload, and audio reconnects by itself if the output drops.
